name: Scholarships and Scams
title: Scholarships and Scams
answer: Scholarships and Scams is about helping students find legitimate college money while avoiding fraudulent offers. Counselors can guide families to trusted scholarship sources, and AI can help organize applications, but students must write their own applications and verify any scholarship before sharing information or paying. The idea matters because scams can cost families money and personal data, and AI can make fake opportunities more convincing.

sections.body: The idea pairs scholarship search support with scam prevention. Students can use large scholarship databases and state aid sites, with counselors helping them find awards that match their situation. AI can assist with tracking deadlines and organizing application materials, but the student remains the author of each application. The problem it solves is twofold: students may miss real aid, and families may fall for services that charge fees, promise guaranteed awards, or collect personal information through fake scholarships. By treating verification as part of the search, schools help students pursue college funding without exposing themselves to fraud.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a school or classroom, counselors can help students identify scholarships from BigFuture and state aid websites, and AI tools can help students organize applications and deadlines. Students write each application in their own words. Counselors should warn families every year about warning signs such as fees to find scholarships, guaranteed awards, and requests for sensitive financial information from unknown organizations. Students should verify any scholarship through a counselor or an official source before applying. Schools can keep a list of verified scholarships and update it regularly, though the text does not give grade bands for this practice.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no evidence label, study, figure, or finding for this idea. It describes scholarship scams as a real risk and notes that AI tools can make scams worse by producing convincing fake websites and messages. Because the supplied text offers no research citation, this idea rests on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Families should never pay to apply for a scholarship or share sensitive financial information with an unknown organization. Students should verify any scholarship through their counselor or an official source before applying. Counselors carry the responsibility to warn families about warning signs every year. Schools can maintain a regularly updated list of verified scholarships to protect families and save students time. The decisions about which scholarships to pursue and what personal information to share stay with the student and family, with counselor guidance.
